carrier.T_rig_tcp_is_T_cube_tcp: same field, different rig: the tracked frame here is the carrier's CAD frame
carrier.tcp_link: carrier_socket_centre (the seated ball centre; no URDF chain involved)
carrier.translation_source: CAD: the seating socket sphere centre sits on the part-studio origin (12.68 mm radius, STEP face #1318), so the rig frame is the TCP frame and the translation is zero by construction, not by fit
carrier.rotation_source: convention, not measurement: z_tcp = z_rig because the socket opens along -z_rig and a ball seats from that side, which is the gripper's body->TCP->table direction -z_tcp; x_tcp = x_rig because the boom is the only distinguished direction left in the plane. A rig with no fingers has no measured roll to inherit.

mount.note: no gripper in this chain. The cube bundles carry this field because a seated ball sits some distance beyond the closed fingers; here the seated ball centre is the TCP itself, so the offset is zero by definition rather than by a caliper.

open_items: the rotation is a convention pinned to the seating direction and the boom, not a measurement; pin it deliberately before mixing carrier episodes with cube-labelled ones

the 0.7 mm sigma is the built part's body scale (-4541 ppm over a 134.8 mm lever arm), measured against CAD on one capture and confounded with the extrinsics' own scale; a second capture on a different day separates them
remove/reseat repeatability of the socket on its ball has not been captured
